examples.en: After a good sleep, my body feels light.
Now that I've cut down my stuff, the bag feels much lighter.

examples.ko: 운동을 하고 나면 몸이 가뿐하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: After exercising, my body feels light and fresh.
I started the new semester with a light heart.

examples.ko: 여행 가방이 가뿐해서 한 손으로 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: The travel bag is light, so I can carry it with one hand.

examples.ko: 몸이 가뿐하지 않으면 오늘은 일찍 쉬세요.
examples.en: If you don't feel light and well, rest early today.

explain: 물건이 가벼운 것뿐 아니라 몸이나 기분이 개운하고 가벼울 때도 써요. '가볍다'와 달리 기분 좋은 느낌이 담겨 있어서 좋은 뜻으로 많이 써요. 반대는 '무겁다'예요.

phrases.en: I feel light and refreshed after exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 개운한 기분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing a refreshed mood.

phrases.en: He lifted the heavy box with ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들이지 않고 쉽게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is done easily, without strain.

phrases.example: 어제 못 자서 오늘은 몸이 가뿐하지 않아요.
phrases.en: I didn't sleep well yesterday, so my body doesn't feel light today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 무겁고 피곤할 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for when the body feels heavy and tired.

explain_en: It covers both a light object and a body or mood that feels fresh and light. Unlike '가볍다', it carries a pleasant feeling, so it is mostly used in a positive sense. The opposite is '무겁다'.

en: dead skin cells; keratin; horny substance

examples.en: In winter, dead skin easily builds up on my heels.
I scrubbed off dead skin at the bathhouse.

examples.ko: 각질 제거 후에는 로션을 꼭 발라요.
examples.en: After removing dead skin, I always put on lotion.

examples.ko: 피부에 각질이 일어나서 화장이 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.en: My skin is flaking, so makeup doesn't go on well.

examples.ko: 손톱 옆 각질을 억지로 뜯으면 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts if you force off the dead skin beside your nail.
Moisturizing is important for skin with a lot of flaking.

explain: 각질은 피부 겉에서 죽어서 떨어져 나가는 세포예요. '각질이 일어나다', '각질을 제거하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요. '때'는 몸에 쌓인 먼지와 땀 같은 것이라 각질과 달라요.

phrases.en: My lips are dry, and the dead skin is peeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부가 건조해서 겉이 일어날 때 '일어나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 일어나다 when dry skin starts to peel up.

phrases.example: 일주일에 한 번 각질 제거를 해요.
phrases.en: I remove dead skin once a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부 관리에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in skin care.

phrases.en: Taking care of dead skin on your feet is important in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 각질이 생기지 않게 돌보는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means caring for skin so dead skin doesn't build up.

explain_en: 각질 is dead cells on the skin's surface that flake away. It is paired with set verbs, 각질이 일어나다 and 각질을 제거하다. 때 (grime) is dust and sweat built up on the body, so it differs from 각질.

en: to roll up; to tuck up

examples.en: He rolled up his sleeves and started washing the dishes.
It was hot, so I rolled my pants up to my knees.

examples.ko: 아버지가 소매를 걷어붙이시더니 짐을 번쩍 드셨어요.
examples.en: Dad rolled up his sleeves and lifted the luggage in one go.
It was raining, so I rolled up my pant legs and walked.

examples.ko: 물이 튀지 않게 소매를 걷어붙이고 손을 씻었어요.
examples.en: I rolled up my sleeves and washed my hands so they wouldn't get splashed.
The way he rolled up his sleeves looked reliable.

explain: 소매나 바짓단을 위로 접어 올릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일을 시작하기 전의 동작이라서 의욕적으로 일에 나서는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '걷다'나 '걷어 올리다'도 써요.

phrases.en: Citizens rolled up their sleeves and got to work cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 소매를 걷는 것이 아니라, 어떤 일에 적극적으로 나선다는 뜻으로 써요. '소매를 걷어붙이다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not literally mean rolling up sleeves but jumping into a task actively. '소매를 걷어붙이다' is said as well.

explain_en: It is used for folding sleeves or pant legs upward. Since it is the motion before starting work, it is also used for jumping into a task with energy. '걷다' and '걷어 올리다' can be used in the same sense.

examples.en: The child suffered from a high fever all night.
I had a high fever, so I went to the hospital.
I couldn't go to school because of a high fever.
The high fever hasn't gone down for three days.

examples.ko: 고열과 기침이 같이 오면 검사를 받으세요.
examples.en: If you get a high fever along with a cough, get tested.

examples.ko: 고열 환자는 물을 많이 마셔야 해요.
examples.en: A patient with a high fever must drink a lot of water.

explain: 일상에서는 '열이 많이 나다'라고 말하고, '고열'은 병원이나 뉴스처럼 좀 더 정확하게 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 열은 '미열'이라고 해요. '고열이 나다', '고열에 시달리다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The child has a high fever.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '고열'보다 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, people say this instead of 고열.

phrases.en: If you have a high fever, go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 병원 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in notices and hospital talk.

phrases.en: I have a high fever and a cough together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 증상과 함께 말할 때 '고열과'로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Link it with other symptoms using 고열과.

explain_en: In daily life people say '열이 많이 나다', and '고열' is used in hospitals and news where the speech is more precise. A slight fever is '미열'. It is often used as '고열이 나다' or '고열에 시달리다'.

examples.en: The toes of my shoes were scuffed, so I applied shoe polish.
There's dust on the toes of my shoes.
The toes of my shoes got soaked because of the rain.
Shoes with pointed toes hurt my feet.
I tripped on the threshold and scuffed the toe of my shoe.
Before the interview, I polished my shoe toes until they shone.

explain: 구두의 앞쪽 끝부분을 말해요. 운동화에는 보통 '신발 앞코'라고 해요. '구두코가 닳다', '구두코가 뾰족하다'처럼 모양과 상태를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I've worn them for a long time, so the toes of my shoes are worn out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 신어서 모양이 변했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when long wear has changed the shape.

phrases.example: 이 구두는 구두코가 뾰족해서 발이 불편해요.
phrases.en: These shoes have pointed toes, so my feet feel uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구두의 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape of a shoe.

phrases.en: The toe of my sneakers got dirty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동화 같은 신발의 앞쪽 끝부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the front tip of shoes like sneakers.

explain_en: It is the front tip of a dress shoe. For sneakers, people usually say '신발 앞코'. It is used to describe the shape or condition, as in '구두코가 닳다' or '구두코가 뾰족하다'.

examples.en: Earlobes quickly turn red when it's cold.
I put a small earring on my earlobe.
My mom fiddles with her earlobe when she's nervous.

examples.ko: 귓불이 두툼하면 복이 많다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that thick earlobes mean good fortune.
The tip of my earlobe feels strangely itchy.
Please gently massage the earlobes too.

explain: 귀의 아래쪽에 말랑하게 늘어진 부분이에요. 귀걸이를 다는 곳이라 '귀걸이'와 함께 자주 나와요. 얼굴이 빨개질 때 '귓불까지 빨개졌다'고도 말해요.

phrases.en: My earlobes turned red from embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부끄럽거나 추울 때 귓불의 색이 변하는 걸 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes earlobes changing color from shyness or cold.

phrases.en: I have a habit of touching my earlobe when I'm nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 귓불을 만지는 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of touching your earlobe with your hand.

phrases.en: A baby's earlobes are soft and squishy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귓불의 느낌을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how an earlobe feels.

explain_en: It's the soft hanging part at the bottom of the ear. Since it's where earrings go, it often appears with '귀걸이'. When someone blushes, people say '귓불까지 빨개졌다'.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나니 눈곱이 잔뜩 끼어 있었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, my eyes were full of sleep.
I washed my face and wiped off the eye gunk.
My puppy often gets eye discharge.
I rushed out without even wiping the sleep from my eyes.

examples.ko: 눈이 아프고 눈곱이 많이 나와서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My eyes hurt and there was a lot of discharge, so I went to the hospital.
You have some sleep in your eye.

explain: 눈 가장자리에 끼는 것을 말하고, 보통 '눈곱이 끼다', '눈곱을 떼다'로 써요. 아침에 자주 보이지만 눈병이 나면 많이 나오기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람에게 미안한 마음이 눈곱만큼도 없어요.
phrases.en: He doesn't feel the slightest bit sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈곱'이 아주 작은 것이라서 '조금도 없다'는 강한 부정을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since eye gunk is tiny, this strongly means 'not even a little'.

explain_en: It is the gunk that collects at the edge of the eye, usually used as '눈곱이 끼다' or '눈곱을 떼다'. You see it often in the morning, but it can increase when you have an eye infection.

examples.en: There was an accident, but he walked out unharmed.

examples.ko: 어제 아팠던 친구가 오늘은 멀쩡히 학교에 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend who was sick yesterday came to school today looking totally fine.

examples.ko: 잘 되던 컴퓨터가 멀쩡히 있다가 갑자기 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: The computer, which had been working fine, suddenly shut off.
Even though I dropped it, the phone turns on just fine.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말을 했어요.
examples.en: He sat there straight-faced and lied.
The child fell but got up fine and laughed.

explain: 멀쩡히는 다치거나 고장 날 것 같은 상황인데도 아무 문제가 없다는 느낌이 강해요. '멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다'처럼 뻔뻔한 태도를 탓할 때도 써요. 사고, 병, 고장 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: It was a big accident, but he is alive and well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 일을 겪고도 아무 문제 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is fine after something dangerous.

phrases.example: 아이가 다친 곳 없이 멀쩡하게 돌아왔어요.
phrases.en: The child came back safe and sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀쩡하게'는 '멀쩡히'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 멀쩡하게 means almost the same and is common in conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to come back safe and sound

phrases.en: Why throw away something that works fine?
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀쩡하다'를 명사 앞에 붙이면 고장 나지 않은 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective before a noun means it's in perfect condition.

explain_en: 멀쩡히 stresses that something is fine even though you would expect harm or breakage. It is also used to blame shameless behavior, as in 멀쩡히 앉아서 거짓말하다. It often appears in stories about accidents, illness, or breakdowns.

examples.en: I fell and my knees were covered in scrapes.
I held the cat and now my hands are covered in scratches.

examples.ko: 축구를 하고 온 아들은 온몸이 상처투성이였어요.
examples.en: My son came back from soccer with scrapes all over his body.
His heart is already full of wounds.
I walked to the end on my badly scarred feet.
I took my scratched-up car in for repair.

explain: '-투성이'는 어떤 것이 가득 묻거나 많은 모양을 나타내요. '흙투성이', '먼지투성이', '피투성이'처럼 쓰여요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이나 물건에도 비유로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 상처투성이 손을 보고 마음이 아팠어요.
phrases.en: Seeing his hands covered in cuts made my heart ache.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 한 부분이 상처로 가득할 때 뒤에 명사를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach a noun after it when a body part is full of injuries.

phrases.en: The child came home covered in scrapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로'를 붙여서 그런 모습으로 어디에 온다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -로, it describes arriving somewhere in that condition.

phrases.en: After the breakup, my heart is full of wounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 아픔을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for emotional pain.

explain_en: '-투성이' shows that something is covered with or full of a thing, as in '흙투성이', '먼지투성이' and '피투성이'. It can be used for bodies and also figuratively for hearts or objects.

examples.en: I put on cream right after washing my face.
I wash my face in the morning with lukewarm water.
My skin got better after I changed my cleanser.
When I finish washing my face, I dry it with a soft towel.
Skin care starts with proper face washing.
When I travel, I keep my face washing simple.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '세수'를 훨씬 자주 말해요. '세안'은 화장품 광고나 피부 관리 이야기에서 나와요. 그래서 '세안제', '클렌징'과 같이 쓰이는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I use a gentle face wash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세안할 때 쓰는 제품이에요. '세안'과 가장 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The product used for washing the face. It is the most common partner of '세안'.

phrases.example: 피부에 맞는 세안 방법을 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm looking for a face-washing method that suits my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피부 관리 이야기에서 어떻게 씻는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in skincare talk about how to wash the face.

phrases.en: I washed my face after waking up in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세안'과 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '세안', but much more natural in everyday talk.

explain_en: In daily conversation, people say 세수 much more often. 세안 appears in cosmetics ads and skin-care talk, so it often goes with words like 세안제 and 클렌징.

examples.en: My lower tooth was loose, so I went to the dentist.
One of my lower teeth fell out yesterday.
The child laughs showing the lower teeth.
My lower and upper teeth don't fit together well.
It hurts a bit when I brush my lower teeth.
I had a lower tooth pulled at the dentist.

explain: 반대말은 '윗니'예요. 소리 나는 대로 [아랜니]라고 읽어요. 이가 빠졌을 때 아이에게는 '아랫니'와 '윗니'를 나눠 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Brush both your upper and lower teeth clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '윗니'와 함께 써서 위아래를 모두 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite '윗니' to mean both upper and lower teeth.

phrases.en: The baby's lower teeth came in first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 이가 올라올 때는 '나다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '나다' when a new tooth comes in.

phrases.en: I brush my lower teeth first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이를 닦는 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about the order of brushing teeth.

explain_en: Its opposite is '윗니' (upper tooth). It is pronounced [아랜니]. People often distinguish '아랫니' and '윗니', for example when a child loses a tooth.

en: to shut one's teeth; to set one's teeth

examples.ko: 그 사람을 잊겠다고 다짐하며 이를 악물었어요.
examples.en: I clenched my teeth, resolving to forget that person.
Even though it hurt, I gritted my teeth and ran to the end.
I keep clenching my teeth, so my jaw hurts.

examples.ko: 눈물이 나는 걸 이를 악물고 참았어요.
examples.en: I held back my tears by gritting my teeth.
This time I will study with all my determination.
Don't clench your teeth; relax.

explain: 거의 '이를 악물다', '어금니를 악물다'처럼 이와 함께 써요. 정말 이를 꽉 무는 동작도 되고, 힘든 일을 참거나 굳게 결심하는 모습을 말할 때도 많이 써요. '악물고'로 이어서 뒤에 오는 동작을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: gritting one's teeth
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아프거나 마음이 힘들어도 참고 해내려는 의지가 강할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone endures pain or hardship with strong determination to get through it.

explain_en: It is almost always used with 이 (teeth), as in '이를 악물다' or '어금니를 악물다'. It can mean really clenching your teeth, but it is also often used for enduring something hard or making a firm resolve. The form '악물고' is often used to describe the action that follows.

examples.en: My knee that I fell on is throbbing with pain.
My tooth is throbbing because of a cavity.

examples.ko: 밤새 상처가 욱신욱신해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The wound throbbed all night, so I couldn't sleep.
After walking for a long time, my legs ache.
The wounded area throbs and feels hot.

examples.ko: 어제 운동한 뒤로 어깨가 욱신욱신 아파요.
examples.en: My shoulder has been aching since I worked out yesterday.

explain: 찌르듯이 계속 쑤시는 아픔을 나타내요. 동사 '욱신거리다'나 '욱신욱신하다'로도 자주 말하고, '쑤시다'와 함께 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My head is throbbing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '욱신욱신'을 동사로 바꾼 말이라서 문장 끝에 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 욱신욱신, so you can end a sentence with it.

phrases.en: My shoulder aches with a throbbing pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 쑤시는 아픔을 더 생생하게 말할 때 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 쑤시다 to describe aching pain more vividly.

phrases.en: My tooth was throbbing, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해서'로 이어서 아픈 이유를 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easy to connect with -해서 to give the reason for going somewhere.

explain_en: It describes a pain that keeps stabbing or throbbing. It is also often used as the verbs '욱신거리다' or '욱신욱신하다', and it goes well with '쑤시다' (to ache).

en: to shrink; to withdraw; to hunch

examples.en: It's cold, so my shoulders hunch up on their own.
I was startled by the loud noise and shrank back.
I keep losing my nerve because of the presentation.
I always end up shrinking in front of the teacher.
It's natural to shrink back from fear of failure.

examples.ko: 경기가 안 좋아서 소비가 움츠러들고 있어요.
examples.en: The economy is bad, so spending is shrinking.

explain: 몸이 오므라들 때뿐 아니라 마음이나 기운이 작아질 때도 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '움츠러드는', '움츠러드니까'가 돼요. 스스로 몸을 오므리는 동작은 '움츠리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: In winter my body shrinks up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추위나 놀람 때문에 몸이 저절로 오므라들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body curls up by itself from cold or fright.

phrases.en: I lost my nerve when I stood in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 기운이 작아지는 느낌을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a feeling of losing spirit or confidence.

phrases.en: Don't shrink back even if you make a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신감이 없어진 사람에게 힘을 주는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to encourage someone who feels timid.

explain_en: It is used both when the body curls up and when courage or energy shrinks. The 'ㄹ' drops in forms like '움츠러드는' and '움츠러드니까'. The deliberate action of pulling your body in is '움츠리다'.

examples.en: The nurse found a vein in my arm.
They drew blood from a vein for the blood test.
Veins are the path blood takes back to the heart.
Veins were bulging in my legs, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 정맥 주사를 맞으면 약이 빨리 퍼져요.
examples.en: With an intravenous shot, the medicine spreads fast.
The veins on the back of my hand look blue.

explain: 피가 심장으로 돌아가는 혈관이에요. 심장에서 나오는 혈관은 '동맥'이라고 해서 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요. 일상에서는 '핏줄'이라고도 하는데, '핏줄'은 가족 관계를 뜻하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I got an intravenous injection at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혈관에 놓는 주사를 말하는 병원 용어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medical term for an injection into a vein.

phrases.en: An artery is a blood vessel that carries blood out of the heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정맥'과 짝으로 외우는 반대 개념이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The paired opposite of 정맥.

phrases.en: I can see blood vessels on the back of my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 혈관을 부르는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday, easy word for blood vessel.

explain_en: The blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart. Its pair is '동맥' (artery), the vessel leaving the heart. In daily speech '핏줄' is also used, though '핏줄' can mean blood relatives too.

examples.en: I pointed toward the road with my index finger.
My index finger got caught in the door, and it hurts.
I picked up the bean with my index finger and thumb.

examples.ko: 아이가 집게손가락을 입술에 대고 조용히 하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child put an index finger to the lips and told us to be quiet.
I put a ring on my index finger.
I got a small cut on my index finger from a knife.

explain: 엄지 옆 손가락이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '검지'라고 짧게 말하는 경우가 많고, '둘째손가락'이라고도 해요. 물건을 집거나 가리킬 때 쓰는 손가락이라서 '집게'라는 말이 붙었어요.

phrases.en: The child pointed at the sky with his index finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 가리킬 때 쓰는 손가락이라는 점이 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that this is the finger used for pointing.
phrases.en_equiv: to point with the index finger

phrases.en: I hurt my index finger while cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손가락 이름을 정확히 말해야 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you need to name the exact finger.

phrases.en: I picked up the bean with my thumb and index finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 손가락으로 물건을 집는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes picking something up with two fingers.

explain_en: It is the finger next to the thumb. In everyday talk people often say the shorter '검지', and '둘째손가락' also exists. It is the finger used to pick things up or point, which is where '집게' comes from.

examples.en: The intestines are several meters long.

examples.ko: 먹은 음식은 위를 지나 창자에 도착해요.
examples.en: Food passes through the stomach and arrives at the intestines.

examples.ko: 소의 창자로 만든 요리를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a dish made from cow intestines.
The intestines absorb nutrients from digested food.

examples.ko: 배가 아파서 창자 쪽이 꼬이는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt, and it felt like my insides were twisting.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 창자 검사를 받으라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to get my intestines examined.

explain: '장'은 병원이나 건강 이야기에서, '창자'는 일상 대화나 음식 이야기에서 많이 써요. 작은창자는 '소장', 큰창자는 '대장'이라고 해요. '창자가 끊어지다'처럼 슬픔을 아주 강하게 말하는 표현에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 아들을 잃은 어머니는 창자가 끊어질 듯 울었어요.
phrases.en: The mother who lost her son cried as if her heart were breaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견디기 힘든 슬픔이나 아픔을 아주 강하게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very strong way to express unbearable sorrow or pain.

explain_en: 장 is used more in hospitals and health topics, while 창자 is used more in everyday talk and food topics. The small intestine is 소장 and the large intestine is 대장. 창자 also appears in strong expressions of grief such as 창자가 끊어지다.

en: to be powerful; to be energetic

examples.en: Grandfather is over eighty, but he's still full of energy.
After a good sleep, my body feels full of energy.
I bought a lively fresh fish at the market.
Kids get full of energy when it's time to play.
I'm still full of life, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 감기가 다 나아서 요즘은 팔팔하게 지내요.
examples.en: My cold is all gone, so I've been doing great lately.

explain: '건강하다'보다 기운이 넘치고 생생하다는 느낌이 강하고, 나이 든 분이나 살아 있는 생선에도 자주 써요. 보통 몸이 튼튼하고 활기 있을 때 말해요. 높임은 '팔팔하세요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Grandmother is still full of energy even though she is quite old.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신께 쓰는 높임형이에요. 기운이 넘치는 모습을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for elders, used to praise someone's lively energy.

phrases.en: I bought lively, fresh fish at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살아서 힘차게 움직이는 생선을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for fish that are alive and moving vigorously.

phrases.example: 아침 운동을 해서 그런지 오늘 팔팔해 보여요.
phrases.en: Maybe because you exercised this morning, you look full of energy today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 판단할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보이다' expresses a judgment based on appearance.

explain_en: It feels more full of vigor than '건강하다' and is often said of elders or live fresh fish. It describes a body that is strong and lively. The honorific form is '팔팔하세요'.

examples.en: I burned my tongue on the hot soup.
The child stuck out his tongue and laughed.
The puppy licked my hand with its tongue.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 혓바닥만 길고 행동은 안 해요.
examples.en: That person is all talk and doesn't take action.
After eating the candy, my tongue turned blue.
The doctor told me to stick out my tongue.

explain: '혀'보다 속되고 거친 느낌이 있어서, 격식 있는 자리나 병원 설명에서는 '혀'를 써요. 귀엽게 말하거나 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때, 또는 말만 앞서는 사람을 낮춰 말할 때 나와요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.example: 병원에서 의사가 혀를 보여 달라고 했어요.
phrases.en: At the hospital, the doctor asked me to show my tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '혀'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'hyeo' at hospitals and in formal settings.

phrases.en: The snake flicked its tongue, so I was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뱀이나 아이처럼 혀를 재빨리 내밀었다 넣는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a tongue flicking in and out, like a snake's.

phrases.en: I ate something spicy, so my tongue is numb and stinging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편한 대화에서 맵거나 뜨거워서 혀가 아픈 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual way to say the tongue stings from spicy or hot food.

explain_en: It sounds cruder than '혀', so in formal situations or medical explanations people use '혀'. It shows up in casual talk among friends, when speaking playfully, or when putting down someone who is all talk. Avoid it with elders.
